messages:
marta: Heads-up — we hit sustained GPU saturation in us-west-2 during the afternoon batch window and the current admission policy is dropping ~12% of incoming requests. Can we discuss switching from hard rejects to a degrade-or-queue fallback?
sam: Saw the spike in the dashboard. p95 token latency jumped too. Drops are mostly from the small-tier rate limiter hitting capacity.
elin: +1 to discussion. Rejects are noisy for customers. Degrade could mean routing to the quantized variants or returning partial tokens? We need clear SLOs.
jess: Quick summary of options: 1) Reject (current) — immediate failure, clear QoS but bad UX. 2) Degrade — route to q4/q8 models or shorter max_tokens. 3) Queue — accept and hold, adds latency and complex backpressure.
marta: For context: the Dedicated pools are at 95% util for 3h windows, auto-scale didn't kick due to cap on reserved GPUs. Cost team flagged more scale as expensive. So soft-degrade seems appealing.
sam: Metrics we care about: drop_rate, p50/p95 latency, queue_length, error_budget burn. Also cost delta for switching 10% of requests to quantized = ~18% token cost reduction.
elin: Proposal sketch: keep a small token-level queue (max_wait=3s, max_queue_len=2000) + degrade when queue is full. Policy config: 
```
admission_policy:
  mode: degrade_then_queue
  degrade_targets: ["gpt-mini-q8", "gpt-micro-q4"]
  max_queue_len: 2000
  max_wait_ms: 3000
  reject_threshold: 0.15 # if backpressure still high
```
This keeps latency bounded but reduces rejects.
jess: I like that. Need to think about KV cache alignment — if we degrade to a different model, latency for initial tokens could spike because of different warm caches. Also need a fallback when quantized model errors increase.
marta: Good call. Add canary rollout: 1% traffic for 2h, monitor token loss and customer error reports. If error_rate increases > 0.5% above baseline revert.
ops-bot: incident:capacity-alert triggered by cluster-monitor at 2026-03-15T15:10Z — mem pressure on node pool gpu-pool-west-2a.
sam: Ops: can we relax reserved cap temporarily to let autoscaler add 2 nodes? Cost billing owner approved emergency credits for two nodes for 6hrs.
elin: Still want the policy change even with scale — it's about graceful degradation not just capacity. Queue-only would create head-of-line latency for high-priority routes.
jess: Suggest mapping priorities: high-priority routes => queue + no degrade (until longer wait), mid => degrade_then_queue, low => immediate degrade or soft-reject. That way enterprise customers get QoS.
marta: Agree. Also add a per-customer token budget check so a single noisy tenant doesn't fill the queue. Add circuit breaker: if tenant_queue_fraction > 0.4 then start per-tenant rejects.
sam: Implementation notes: router change is small (policy toggle + target list), but need rollout in control-plane + runtime. Runtime supports model substitution via alias but we need to add metrics tags for degraded=true.
elin: Monitoring: add new dashboards for degraded_rate, queue_time_ms histogram, per-model error_rate. Alert thresholds: degraded_rate > 20% for 10m => page oncall.
oncall: Oncall escalation policy: page oncall if p99 latency > 5s OR drop_rate > 5% OR degraded_rate > 25% sustained 10m.
marta: Plan: 1) PR with policy + config (sam/elin) 2) small canary (1%) for 2h 3) extend to 10% if stable 4) region rollout us-west-2 then eu-west-1. Sam/Elin can own. 5) ops to scale nodes if we cross 96% again.
sam: I'll open a PR and add the config snippet + unit tests for routing logic.
elin: I'll add dashboard panels and a synthetic test that simulates queue saturation.
jess: I'll update the runbook with degrade semantics and customer comms template (we should notify customers about potential mild quality changes).
marta: Thanks all. If we see any regression during canary -> revert flag is `admission.mode=reject` and `degraded=false` in runtime.
sam: PR: 1764010045 — adding policy + tests.\/cc @ops-bot for scaling.
ops-bot: scale_request: approved, adding 2 g4dn nodes to gpu-pool-west-2a (ETA 4m)
marta: Closing loop — let's sync tomorrow 09:30 UTC to review canary metrics. :thumbsup:
